title: WORKDIR
definition: The instruction that sets the working directory (the active folder) for any subsequent `RUN`, `CMD`, `ENTRYPOINT`, `COPY`, and `ADD` instructions that follow it in the Dockerfile.
simpleExplanation: Typing `cd` (change directory) in the terminal. It tells Docker 'For the rest of the recipe, do all your work inside this specific folder'.
realWorldExample: `WORKDIR /app`. Now, if the next line is `COPY . .`, it copies your files directly into the `/app` folder. If you open a terminal in the live container later, you will start inside the `/app` folder.

basic: What happens if you set a `WORKDIR` to a folder that doesn't exist yet?
intermediate: Why is using `WORKDIR /app` better than just writing `RUN cd /app`?

answers.question: Folder doesn't exist?
answers.answer: Docker will automatically create the folder for you.

answers.question: Why better than cd?
answers.answer: Because every `RUN` instruction happens in complete isolation. If you write `RUN cd /app` on line 4, Docker changes the directory, finishes the layer, and then *immediately forgets it*. Line 5 will be back in the root directory. `WORKDIR` makes the change permanent for the whole file.
